chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man performed Zihar, then had intercourse before he expiated. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: Is this not how the Faqih (jurist) acts?

key_terms.الْفَقِيهُ: Al-Faqih: The jurist or understanding man.
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Zihar: A form of divorce where a husband declares his wife to his back like his mother's back.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zihar if the husband has intercourse before expiating?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the juristic consensus that sexual intercourse prior to expiation does not nullify the Zihar bond, thereby keeping the obligation of kaffarah intact. This highlights the precision of Shia fiqh in distinguishing between the act of intercourse and the formal revocation of the prohibition, ensuring the husband remains bound to the prescribed expiation. The Imam’s rhetorical question underscores the reliability of the established legal precedent derived from the Quranic injunctions on Zihar.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man did Zahaar, then copulated before he expiated. So heasws said to me: ‘Is this not how the understanding man (Faqih) acts?’
en.sarwar: 30. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who expresses the statement of al-Zihar about his wife, then goes to bed with her before paying expiation. He (the Imam) said, ’Is it not the way a faqih (scholar of law) man does? 5 ”
